title: Flash tabs: auto-cleanup kept tabs after idle timeout

brief.why: The --keep-tab decision is a constant source of confusion. Default mode destroys the tab (user can't see results). Keep-tab leaves orphan tabs that accumulate. brief.what: 1. ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINT: passe is a single-shot CLI — no daemon, process exits after script. Timer must either be Chrome-side or a detached background process 2. Option C: simpler — just document keep-tab cleanup as a separate manual step and add 'passe close-tabs' command to clean up orphans 5. Evaluate options before implementing — this may not be worth the complexity
brief.done: passe run --flash keeps tab for 30s then auto-closes. New passe run closes old flash tab. User interaction cancels timer. No orphan tab accumulation. Test coverage for timer and cancellation.

title: Inline JS block syntax for eval verbs (triple-angle delimiters)

brief.why: The eval-file dance is the root cause of monster one-liners. Claudes instinctively inline JS because eval-file requires two tool calls (Write JS file, then run script referencing it). Even the 'with skill' Sonnet wrote the minified IIFE first, then self-corrected. The DSL is line-based but JS is multi-line — this structural mismatch produces the #1 anti-pattern (943 occurrences).
brief.what: 1. PARSER STATE CHANGE: parse_script() is currently a stateless line-by-line loop. Adding block delimiters means adding state (in_block flag, collected lines, target verb+args). Restructure parse_script to handle blocks 2. Syntax: 'eval-to /tmp/data.json <<<' starts a block, '>>>' on its own line ends it. Collected lines joined with newline as the expression arg 3. Edge case: JS unsigned right shift operator (>>>) — require >>> to be on its own line with no other content to disambiguate 4. Only works in heredoc and .passe files — -c mode rejects <<< with clear error suggesting heredoc 5. Works for eval, eval-to, assert (all RAW_REST_VERBS and RAW_REST_AFTER_PATH_VERBS)
brief.done: A .passe script or heredoc can contain 'eval-to /tmp/data.json <<<' followed by multi-line JS followed by '>>>' and it executes correctly. Parser test coverage. -c mode with <<< emits a clear error suggesting heredoc.

brief.why: Usage analysis found Claude wrote 'wait 500'/'wait 1000'/'wait 1500' guesses ~6 times across sessions. Every one is a proxy for 'wait until the page has finished its XHR/fetch calls.' Idle = in-flight count reaches zero and stays zero for 500ms (debounce prevents premature exit on request waterfalls) 4. If Network.enable already active (capture verb), reuse without double-enabling 5. Register 'wait-idle' in KNOWN_VERBS, wire into run_script dispatch 6. Add optional timeout_ms arg (default 30s) 7. Emit {"verb":"wait-idle","ms":...,"settled_after_ms":N} in step NDJSON 8. Update CLAUDE.md verb reference and footguns section (document SPA click-navigation gap + wait-idle as the fix)

title: Screenshot survives long CDP sessions without compositor timeout

brief.why: Brisk-bear reported screenshot timeouts after sustained CDP use. Investigation found three issues: (1) PASSE_CDP pointed at remote Mac Chrome via tailscale — DPR=2 Retina meant 4× pixels plus multi-MB base64 over network, misidentified as compositor stalls. (2) CDPClient.send had a hardcoded 15s timeout — too short for full-page screenshots of dense pages on software-rendered headless Chrome (Wikipedia NASA: 136s at DPR=1). (3) Headless Chromium on kube was using software rasterisation despite a GTX 1650 SUPER being available — Debian's blocklist disabled GPU.
brief.what: 1. CDPClient.send() accepts per-call timeout parameter (committed) 2. Screenshot capture timeout set to 300s — detect dead browser, don't cap rasterisation (committed) 3. Headless Chrome GPU enabled via --ignore-gpu-blocklist --use-angle=vulkan in systemd service — Wikipedia NASA drops from 136s to 2s (applied to service, documented in CLAUDE.md) 4. Filed passe-zomeca under passe-mofuco — passe should report which Chrome it connects to
brief.done: CDPClient.send accepts timeout parameter. Screenshot uses 300s timeout. Kube headless Chrome GPU-accelerated (2s for Wikipedia NASA). 30-site soak test: 0 failures. CLAUDE.md documents the setup.
